A movement model for the walker

movement_model.Rd

Holds what simulate_tracks() needs to move an animal: a sampler of step lengths, a sampler of turning angles, the time one step takes, and, optionally, a switch between a moving state and a resting state. Any pair of samplers can be supplied, so a model fitted elsewhere, such as the step and turn distributions of a hidden Markov model, can drive the walker. crw_model() builds the common case, a correlated random walk.

Usage

movement_model(
  step,
  turn,
  states = 1,
  transition = NULL,
  time_step_s = 60,
  source = ""
)

Arguments

step

A function of n that returns n step lengths in metres, each the straight-line distance covered in one time step.

turn

A function of n that returns n turning angles in radians, the change of bearing between one step and the next.

states

1 for one moving state, or 2 for a move and rest switch.

transition

For states = 2, a 2 by 2 matrix of transition probabilities between steps. Rows are the state at one step and columns the state at the next, so transition[i, j] is the probability of state j after a step in state i, and each row sums to 1. State 1 is moving and state 2 resting; transition[2, 2] is the probability of resting again after a rest.

time_step_s

Seconds per step.

source

Where the samplers come from, in words. It is printed with the model and kept with every simulation made from it.

Value

An object of class movement_model: a list with elements step, turn, states, transition, time_step (seconds per step) and source.

Details

The walker moves by a sequence of step lengths and turning angles, each drawn from its own probability distribution. The move and rest switch below is a two-state Markov chain between steps, a switch between movement states by a transition matrix as in Morales et al. (2004).

With states = 2, state 1 moves with the two samplers and state 2 rests: the animal stays where it is. The state changes between steps by the transition matrix, so the number of steps spent in state i before a change is geometric with mean 1 / (1 - transition[i, i]).

References

Morales, J. M., Haydon, D. T., Frair, J., Holsinger, K. E. and Fryxell, J. M. (2004). Extracting more out of relocation data: building movement models as mixtures of random walks. Ecology, 85, 2436-2445. doi:10.1890/03-0269 (Switching between behavioural states by a state transition matrix.)

See also

crw_model(), simulate_tracks()

Examples

# Steps of 20 to 40 m per minute and turns of up to 30 degrees either way.
m <- movement_model(
  step = function(n) stats::runif(n, 20, 40),
  turn = function(n) stats::runif(n, -pi / 6, pi / 6),
  time_step_s = 60, source = "uniform steps and turns, for illustration"
)
m
#> <movement_model> 1 state 
#> time step: 60 s
#> source: uniform steps and turns, for illustration

# The same walk, resting for a mean of 10 steps after a mean of 20 moving.
movement_model(
  step = function(n) stats::runif(n, 20, 40),
  turn = function(n) stats::runif(n, -pi / 6, pi / 6),
  states = 2, transition = matrix(c(0.95, 0.10, 0.05, 0.90), 2)
)
#> <movement_model> 2 states (move, rest) 
#> time step: 60 s
#> mean steps in a state: move 20.0, rest 10.0
#> source: not stated
